title: The sunset date cannot move
treatment: Plan to commence on 19 June 2028, a clear month early. Track G10 (resolve to make) as the immovable decision — everything after it is administrative. Report float at every steering group.
note: If the law is not remade by 19 July 2028, every permit trigger, notice power and infringeable offence in the register stops. There is no extension mechanism.

title: Slippage runs into the 2028 election caretaker period
treatment: Hold the making decision at April 2028 with August as the last recoverable date. Confirm the caretaker start with Governance once the VEC publishes it.
note: General elections in October 2028. Major decisions are constrained from roughly late September, so the float after the sunset is illusory.

title: Council meeting cycle compresses the Q1 gates
treatment: Book G2, G9 and G10 into the meeting calendar as soon as it is set, with the report deadline working backwards from the agenda close date.
note: There is no January meeting, and report deadlines close roughly two weeks before each meeting. Two gates sit either side of that gap.

title: Charter of Human Rights challenge to the camping and directive powers
treatment: Start the Charter assessment in phase 1 rather than at drafting. Document the outreach-first operating protocol alongside the clause. Brief counsel early on cl.143.
note: Clauses 143, 120, 149 and 177 are the exposure. Assessment after drafting is too late to change the drafting.

title: Submission volume on cat containment overwhelms the statutory stage
treatment: Do the contested work at the deliberative panel in phase 3, not at exhibition. Resource submission handling for a high-volume scenario and book a dedicated hearing committee.
note: Neighbouring councils have drawn submissions in the thousands on this single question.

title: The three incorporated documents are not reviewed in step with the law
treatment: Run the Footpath Trading Policy, Keeping of Animals Policy and Procedure and Protocol Manual as named workstreams with their own owners and the same gate dates.
note: Clause 19 incorporates all three. If they lag, the new law commences pointing at documents written for the old one.

title: Enforcement data is not good enough to carry an evidence case
treatment: Scope the data extract in phase 2 and find out early what cannot be answered. Where the record is thin, use the pilots to generate the evidence instead.
note: Request and infringement data is held across several systems and clause-level coding is inconsistent.

title: Drafting resource is not secured in time
treatment: Confirm the drafting resource at G1 and start procurement by March 2027. Drafting cannot start later than July 2027 without eating the exhibition window.
note: External drafting has procurement lead time, and a specialist local law drafter is a small market.

title: Overlap with state regimes creates an inconsistency argument
treatment: Legal review of each overlapping clause before drafting instructions. Where the state covers the field, remove rather than restate.
note: Noise against the Environment Protection Regulations 2021, short-stay against the state levy and owners corporation rules, drones against CASA, e-rideables against the Road Safety Road Rules.

title: Pilots run too late to influence the drafting
treatment: Every pilot must close by 30 June 2027 with a written evaluation. A pilot that cannot report by G4 does not start.
note: Drafting instructions are approved at G6 in September 2027. Evidence that arrives after that is evidence for the next review, not this one.

title: Items parked for years reappear after the scope is locked
treatment: Run the held-over surgery at E02 and publish the disposition of every backlog item. After G3, new items go to a register for the next review unless the sponsor takes it to the steering group.
note: Three items in the backlog have been open since 2019 and 2020. The review is the moment they surface.
